h: Tips for a Steamy Day Under Glass
p: A visit here is a bit of a sensory treat. The air is warm and damp, you'll hear water trickling and birds calling, and the smell of earth and leaves hits you the moment you walk in. It's the closest most of us will get to a real jungle without a long-haul flight, and it's a cracking way to spark kids' interest in nature and the wider world.

Dress in layers so you can peel off once you're inside, and if you wear glasses, expect them to steam up for the first few minutes. Pace yourself and look up, down and sideways, because some of the residents are masters of camouflage and are easy to walk straight past. Asking a member of staff where an animal tends to hide can save a lot of fruitless searching.

Older kids often enjoy the sustainability side of things, learning how everyday foods such as chocolate, bananas and coffee grow, and how what we buy affects rainforests on the other side of the world. It makes a great school-project day out.

The surrounding area offers plenty to make a full day or weekend of it. Newbury has the ruins of Donnington Castle, an English Heritage site with a towering medieval gatehouse on a hill just north of town, free to explore. Greenham Common, once a famous airbase, is now open heathland that's great for walks and spotting wildlife. Fans of a certain period drama might fancy Highclere Castle, south of Newbury, which famously starred as Downton Abbey, though it only opens on selected dates. And of course, there are plenty of country pubs scattered around the villages for a relaxed lunch.
